correctness.rationale: For each r>=3 and s>=2, the unit-edge P1 Gram matrix is (2dI+A)/6, with Q=6M eigenvalues 2d, s(2r-3) and 3d on within-part contrasts, part-constant contrasts and constants. Its exact three-entry inverse gives evaluation kernels with signed values (3st+1)beta, beta and -2beta. Exact affine absolute-value integration and all edge multiplicities yield 2+[t(s-4)+1]/[3t(ts+1)]. Negative kernel contribution on a third-part edge makes every interior evaluation strictly smaller. Exact derivatives and limits give threshold, reversal and global extrema. Extracted exact-rational checker performs 10 direct inversions, 526 edge integrations, interior gaps, and 4136 parameter checks; finite checks do not stand in for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the exact arclength L-infinity stability norm on the balanced complete r-partite unit metric graph for r>=3,s>=2, including strict vertex norming, sharp threshold s=4 and reversal of r-monotonicity. Same-claim and broader-implication comparisons against previously documented mathematical claims, publicly indexed mathematical results and three inspected full open-access primary papers found no covering formula. A plausible 2006 finite-element paper was inaccessible beyond abstract and remains a stated risk; negative search alone is not used as novelty proof.

value.rationale: The object is a natural highly symmetric metric-network finite-element approximation family, with sharp L-infinity stability relevant to worst-case amplification of least-squares data. The result determines all norming vertices and the full exact two-parameter constant, not a generic estimate, with a part-size-four threshold independent of the number of classes and a switch in the effect of increasing the class count. The attained minimum 121/63 and unattained supremum 19/9 are meaningful family extremal constants; the result is not inferred by renaming or restricting any identified older formula.
